wi_east_bluff_north.blurb: East Bluff North is the northern end of the East Bluff above Devil's Lake, in Wisconsin's Baraboo Range. It is almost purely bouldering on the lake's quartzite, with talus fields along the upper part of the bluff and a few stray blocks in the woods. Grades start below V0 and are well stocked through V4, then thin out gradually toward a few problems at V10 and above. Monolith Ridge is the standout: a narrow rocky ridge between the lake and the Steinke Creek side, with a wide variety of problems and mostly flat landings. East Bluff North Talus, North Shore and Monolith Talus add plenty more, so there is a lot to do in a single visit.

ab_cougar_canyon_creek.blurb: Cougar Canyon is a creek canyon in the Bow Valley by Canmore, where sport climbing is the whole story. At Planet X the rock is limestone with small holds and technical moves; quality varies, so helmets are wise. Grades are centred on 5.10 and 5.11, with a decent group of 5.8s and 5.9s, and a hard tail of 5.12 through 5.14 for those projecting. House of Cards, Cat's Eye Wall, Planet X and Crowbar Wall are among the biggest crags. The right side of the canyon is shady and the left side sunny, and Planet X stays cool even in summer. Summer and fall are the best seasons, because spring runoff keeps the creek high.

az_homestead_the.blurb: The Homestead is a remote high-desert canyon in Gila County, central Arizona, between Globe and Winkelman. Limestone cliffs line both sides of the canyon, with a dozen or so walls, each with its own style of rock and its own sun exposure. This is a pure sport area, with the weight of the climbing at 5.10 to 5.12 and the busiest band at 5.11, a few easier lines and a handful at 5.13. Finland Terrace, Slate Nation, Tufa City and the Mouse Wall hold the most routes. Summers bring extreme heat, so the cooler months suit it better.

ca_courtright_reservoir.blurb: Courtright Reservoir sits in the Sierra National Forest, roughly two hours east of Fresno, and climbs on granite domes and walls. Friction slabs, steep edging faces and cracks are all here, with trad the largest share, then sport, multi-pitch dome routes, and a good bouldering area. Power Dome is known for long friction climbs, Trapper Dome for bolted slab, and Tiger Cage, Tiger Wall and Voyager Rock for cracks and faces. Grades mostly span 5.6 to 5.12, centred on 5.10 with plenty of 5.7 to 5.9 for newer leaders. Late spring to late fall is the season, and the crags are usually quiet and uncrowded.

ca_horsemen_s_center.blurb: Horsemen's Center is a High Desert sport climbing area at Apple Valley, California, at about 3,200 feet. The granite resembles Joshua Tree: most of it is grainy tan, with smoother brown or grey stone being the best. Routes are short, mostly 25 to 80 feet, and sport leads, with a good number of boulder problems and a fair share of top-rope and trad. Grades run from easy to 5.12, with most between 5.8 and 5.11, and bouldering from the low grades up to about V5. BMX Crags, The Cemetery and Outer Limits are the main groups. The crags are sunny, though exposure varies between them, and winter can be a good escape from cold and wind.

sd_mount_baldy.blurb: Mount Baldy is a granite bouldering area in the Black Hills of South Dakota, near the back of Mount Rushmore. The boulders are scattered widely, with a small amount of sport and trad on the formation itself. Problems start at V0 and are well spread through the middle grades, with a solid group between V3 and V8 and a few at V10 and V11. The granite is hard on the fingertips, and landings are generally good. Old Baldy Frontside, Irie Heights, Camp Judson Road and Baldy's Lil-Brother hold the most problems. Conditions are good most of the year, but summer heat makes it easy to lose skin.
